name: Dig Rat Stew
summary: Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens for the rodents his recipe needs.

sections.title: Barrens Delicacies
sections.body: Hunters cross the dry Barrens in search of zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, wants something else: dig rats. Hungry all day, he offers his recipe to any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents.

sections.title: The Dwarven Vermin
sections.body: Deep in the southern Barrens, dwarven prospectors dig into the red earth at Bael Modan. Their work has disturbed nests of dig rats. The dwarves see an infestation; Grub sees a feast near the excavation.

sections.title: A Matter of Flavor
sections.body: Grub says dig rats taste best after rotting for several weeks. For a hungry traveler who wants food now, he accepts fresher meat. His recipe shows how forgiving roadside cooking can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

faq.answer: Grub is an orc camping along the trail east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Always hungry, he has peculiar tastes and teaches travelers to cook local vermin.

faq.q: Where do dig rats come from?
faq.answer: Dig rats infest Bael Modan, an Alliance excavation in the far southern Barrens, south of Camp Taurajo and north of Razorfen Kraul. Dwarven mining disturbed the ground and brought swarms of the small creatures.

faq.q: Why does Grub want dig rats specifically?
faq.answer: Grub calls dig rats everyone's favorite feast and says hunting vermin is a rite of passage for seasoned travelers. They are the main ingredient in his hearty, pungent stew.

faq.q: Is Dig Rat Stew actually good to eat?
faq.answer: Grub calls the stew delicious, though his taste is extreme. He prefers meat that has rotted for a few weeks, making it an acquired taste even by rugged Horde standards.

faq.q: Why are there dwarves in Bael Modan?
faq.answer: The dwarves of Bael Modan belong to an Ironforge expedition. They built a keep and excavation in the southern Barrens and blast and dig deep into the land. Their presence has heightened tensions with the Horde and stirred up native vermin.

faq.q: Do you need special culinary training to make the stew?
faq.answer: Grub's method calls for basic hearthcraft and field dressing. Anyone with rudimentary cooking experience can learn to simmer the rodents into a sustaining meal.

angles.text: Preparing dig rat stew teaches frontier foraging: vermin become a filling, foul-smelling campfire meal.
Taking dig rats from Bael Modan lets you mock the dwarven excavation while gathering rations in the southern Barrens.
Grub likes to let meat rot for weeks before boiling it, a taste few living cooks share with the Forsaken.
